title: Multiparametric Optical Mapping of the Langendorff-perfused Rabbit Heart
protocol: Prepare freshly made Tyrodes' solution by mixing 1840 mL deionized water with 80 mL Stock I and 80 mL Stock II.
Add 4 g of glucose to the mixture for the Tyrodes' solution.
Store stock solutions of dyes and uncouplers at -20°C or +4°C as specified.
Mix 30 μL di-4-ANEPPS stock solution with experimental setup.
Mix 30 μL RH 237 stock solution with experimental setup.
Mix 200 μL Rhod-2AM stock solution with experimental setup.
Store 100 μL aliquots of di-4-ANEPPS at -20°C to avoid repeated freezing and thawing.
Dissolve blebbistatin in DMSO and store the solution at +4°C.
Transfer Tyrodes' solution into a 2L bottle for the water bath.
Place the bottle in a water bath to maintain the solution temperature at 37 °C.
Oxygenate the solution with 95% O₂ - 5% CO₂.
Maintain the pH of the solution at 7.35±0.05 by adjusting oxygenation level.
Filter the solution using a nylon net filter (pore size: 11 μm) before it enters the perfusion line.
Prepare monitoring equipment for heart harvesting and perfusion.
Adjust the baseline of the pressure transducer to zero mmHg when not attached to the perfusion system.
Place pseudo-ECG electrodes in the chamber to approximate Lead I, II, and III ECG readings.
Fix the rabbit in a restrainer.
Euthanize the rabbit with an intravenous injection of sodium pentobarbital (50 mg/kg) and 2000 U heparin.
Open the thoracic cavity quickly after complete euthanasia.
Excise the heart and lungs from the thoracic cavity.
Make a cut at the upper end of ascending aorta before all branches of aortic arch.
Flush out air from ascending aorta and quickly cannulate heart to a 16-gauge cannula attached to a bubble trapper.
Retrogradely perfuse heart in a non-recirculating Langendorff perfusion system.
Make a cut to open pericardium quickly.
Remove lung, trachea, fat, and connective tissues while blood is flushed out by perfusion.
Insert silicone tubing through pulmonary vein into left ventricle (LV) and keep there throughout experiment.
Move heart with cannula to recirculating Langendorff-perfusion system with optical mapping apparatus.
Place heart in custom-made hexagon chamber and connect cannula to perfusion system.
Maintain aortic pressure at 60 ± 5 mmHg by adjusting flow rate of perfusion pump.
Monitor lead I pseudo-ECG.
Maintain pH around 7.35 ± 0.05.
Turn off the room light.
Slowly inject blebbistatin stock solution through the injection port above the cannula.
Inject 0.1 ml of blebbistatin for every bolus injection.
Wait for pressure to stabilize before each subsequent injection.
Gently place the pacing electrode onto the designated location.
Focus the image of the heart in the frosted glass from three evenly spaced angles.
Adjust the position of the cannula and distances between each PDA and the heart.
Take a picture of each focused image.
Slowly inject 10-20 μL di-4-ANEPPS stock solution through the injection port into the perfusion solution.
Wait 1-3 minutes before taking optical recordings.
Turn the green LED light on for the first recording.
Take optical recordings simultaneously from three PDAs connected with the custom-made data acquisition system.
Turn off the LED light after taking recordings.
Check the quality of signals from different pixels of all three PDAs.
Add 0.1 to 0.2 ml blebbistatin stock solution if motion artifacts in the optical action potential are noticed.
Add another 5 μl di-4-ANEPPS stock solution if signal-to-noise ratio is low.
Re-stain the heart with additional 5 μl di-4-ANEPPS stock solution if the signal deteriorates due to photobleaching or washout.
Turn on the room light after completion of the functional study.
Take pictures of the heart from 36 evenly spaced angles by rotating the heart at a step of 10° with a digital camera fixed at one PDA location.
Take the heart out of the chamber.
Drain all solutions and wash the perfusion system in sequence with DI water, 70% reagent alcohol, and again DI water.
Place the cannulated heart in a glass chamber and connect the cannula to the perfusion system.
Pin down the heart to the silicon bottom of the chamber at the ventricular apex and atria.
Inject blebbistatin stock solution (15˜20 min to reach 10 μM) through the injection port prior to perfusion cannula to immobilize the heart.
Place a plastic Petri dish or glass window cover above the epicardial surface to reduce motion of the solution surface.
Focus two CMOS cameras in the dual mapping system at the same field of view.
Separate emitted fluorescence using a dichroic mirror (635 nm cutoff) and filter it with a 700 nm longpass filter for voltage signals, and by a 590/30 nm bandpass filter for calcium signals.
Aim light guides of two halogen lamps towards the mapping field of view to achieve even illumination using excitation filters (531/40 nm).
Stain the heart with the voltage-sensitive dye RH 237 stock solution (10˜30 μL) through the injection port.
Mix Rhod-2AM stock solution with Pluronic F-127 in a 1:1 ratio.
Sonicate the mixture for 1 minute in a water-bath sonicator.
Inject the mixture through the bubble trapper's port.
Wait approximately 20 minutes to allow de-esterification of Rhod-2 AM before starting mapping.
Turn off the superfusion pump to avoid motion at the surface of the solution.
Turn on the excitation light source (the halogen lamps).
Take optical recordings using both cameras connected to the data acquisition system (Ultima-L, SciMedia).
Turn off the excitation light.
Turn on the superfusion pump.
Check the quality of the optical signals.
Re-stain the tissue if necessary.
Finish the rest of the designed experimental protocol for a study.
Turn on the room light and take a photograph of the heart containing the field of view.
Take the heart out of the chamber.
Drain all the solutions.
Wash the perfusion system in the sequence of DI water, 70% reagent alcohol (Fisher Scientific), and DI water.
